results.title: Hackers Made an App That Kills to Prove a Point | WIRED
results.content: Medtronic and the FDA left an insulin pump with a potentially deadly vulnerability on the market—until researchers who found the flaw showed how bad it could be. Medtronic and the FDA left an insulin pump with a potentially deadly vulnerability on the market—until the researchers who found the flaw showed how bad it could be.Casey Chin; Tony Rusecki/Alamy. Two years ago, researchers Billy Rios and Jonathan Butts discovered disturbing vulnerabilities in Medtronic's popular MiniMed and MiniMed Paradigm insulin pump lines. They built an Android app that could use the flaws to kill people. "We’ve essentially just created a universal remote for every one of these insulin pumps in the world," Rios says. But as Rios and Butts discovered, it's relatively easy to determine the radio frequencies on which the remote and pump talk to each other.

results.title: Enhancing Medication Adherence with an IoT-based Pill Dispenser and ...
results.content: This paper endeavors to offer a comprehensive solution to medication adherence by introducing an IoT-based Smart Pill Dispenser and Smart Cup, coupled with seamless integration with an Android application. Our proposed solution builds upon these works by introducing a comprehensive IoT-based approach, encompassing a Smart Pill Dispenser, Smart Cup, and an Android application for real-time monitoring, notifications, and adherence alerts. SYSTEM DESIGN The system described in this paper encompasses three primary components, as shown in Fig.1: the Pill Dispenser, the Smart Cup, and the Android Application, which collectively form a comprehensive solution for medication management. Additionally, the Pill Dispenser is pivotal in notifying the user by signaling the associated Android application during scheduled medication times. The Android Application receives a notification from the Pill Dispenser, providing a 5-minute advance alert to the user, thereby ensuring timely medication adherence. This test ensured that the Android Application accurately received and synchronized medication schedules and adherence data, reflecting real-time changes made through the Pill Dispenser's user interface.
